extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a comprehensive evaluation benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) as embodied brains in robotic manipulation. It systematically evaluates MLLMs across five dimensions—Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark curates datasets across diverse embodiments (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulation, humanoid), attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation, drawing from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection. It introduces a novel MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework for long-horizon planning that moves beyond symbolic matching to evaluate embodied feasibility.
extraction.creator: Peking University, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Fudan University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Datasets were built from open-source robotic datasets and in-house collection, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Each sub-benchmark aligns with the embodied task pipeline for realism. For instruction comprehension, explicit instructions were drawn from daily-life scenarios and implicit ones obtained by LLM rewriting. For perception, real robot data with metadata was used with template-based QA, GPT-generated functional properties, Gemini-segmented video steps, and human-labeled bounding boxes. For planning, a planning pool was built from high-quality robotic videos with Gemini-generated structured annotations refined by human annotators. For affordance, representative frames from the planning pool were sampled and annotated. For failure analysis, execution-level failures were collected from RoboMIND and labeled by experts, while planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-source robotic datasets including Open X-Embodiment Collaboration, RH20T (Fang et al. 2023), RoboMIND (Wu et al. 2024), AgiBot World Colosseo (Bu et al. 2025), and other robotic video datasets (Lin et al. 2024a; Liu et al. 2024b;c; Mu et al. 2023; Yang et al. 2024), combined with in-house collected data.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Implicit instructions obtained by rewriting explicit instructions into demand-based requests using LLMs. Planning-level failures synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage quality control: (1) data filtering during construction with both general filters (image quality, task validity) and task-specific filters (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); (2) post-construction validation with 20 professionally trained annotators conducting quality inspections (linguistic clarity, answerability, correctness). Majority-vote strategy: items all models solve correctly are removed, items all models fail undergo manual review and correction. Frame sequences extracted from videos as standardized inputs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Gemini generates structured annotations—task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments)—which are refined by human annotators. Each step is mapped into function templates (e.g., pick_up(object), move_to(object, target)) grouped into manipulation or navigation skill lists. Human annotators provide bounding boxes for task-centric perception, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes for spatial/causal reasoning, and annotations for three types of affordance (static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, mobile base positions). Execution-level failures labeled by experts. Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) capturing inter-step dependencies are manually annotated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority-vote strategy used: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. Human evaluation study conducted on 438 long-horizon tasks with Pearson correlation analysis to validate the MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation metric against human judgments.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators recruited for quality inspections. Expert annotators with prior training assigned holistic scores for human evaluation study.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (for video segmentation and structured annotation generation), GPT (for generating functional properties and distractors), LLMs (for rewriting explicit to implicit instructions).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data. Execution-level failure diagnosis remains challenging even for humans (47.30 score). The benchmark evaluation of long-horizon planning depends on MLLM-as-world-simulator which may inherit biases from the underlying MLLM.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation benchmark for MLLMs as embodied brains in robotic manipulation. Used to evaluate five dimensions: Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis. Provides a leaderboard and actionable insights for advancing embodied brain capabilities in robotic AI.
